WHO ARE WE?

San Francisco Public Utilities Commission (SFPUC)

Headquartered in San Francisco, we have 2,300 employees operating across eight counties serving more than 2.7 million customers in the San Francisco Bay Area – 24 hours per day, 365 days per year.

Our Mission:
To provide our customers with high quality, efficient, and reliable water, power, and wastewater services in a manner that values environmental and community interests and sustains the resources entrusted to our care.

Our Vision:
We are an innovative utility leader, recognized for excellent results in service, safety, stewardship, and inclusiveness.

To learn more about working at the SFPUC, visit our career site at https://www.sfpuc.org/about-us/careers-sfpuc

Role Description

Position Summary:

Under general supervision, the 1478- Utility Services Representative performs responsible and specialized journey-level clerical duties in the Water Quality Division in connection with the Cross Connection Control Program. The Cross Connection Control Program was established to identify and address potential concerns with potable water contamination in the public water system where cross connections exist and backflow may occur. Backflow prevention assemblies are installed where various forms of water system cross connections are present, and regulatory compliance consists of annual testing and review by our Environmental Services and Field Services (ES/FS) groups of where these assemblies are installed. This position is dedicated to the Cross Connection Control Program, future Water Quality projects, and will provide support for activities focused on communication with customers and external entities regarding compliance, account information management, tracking and reporting, and coordinating office operations within the Environmental Services and Field Services groups.

Work Location
: 1657 Rollins Road, Burlingame, CA

Schedule
: M-F (in-office), full-time

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Generate notices to account holders for annual backflow assembly test requirements
Interface with customers and testers regarding Cross Connection Control requirements and regulations; monitor and respond to email and voicemail inquiries
Initiate correspondence with the Department of Public Health regarding account holder and tester violations and compliance issues
Initiate correspondence with the Department of Building Inspection regarding permits to install, remove/replace backflow prevention assemblies.
Maintain and reconcile account holder information and records of outgoing notices
Coordinate and compile the sale of backflow prevention tags on a monthly basis; maintain inventory of materials and supplies
Research customer contact information and plumbing permit numbers for new installations
Use web-based applications to monitor and manage account information/status, and generate reports
Participate in testing of web-based applications, reconcile data anomalies
Plan and organize Cross Connection Control Program meetings and prepare agendas/minutes
Monitor Cross Connection Control Program incoming email with the ability to prioritize and balance workload
Collaborate with 7317 Senior Water Service Inspector, ITS and consultants to enhance Cross Connection Control Program webpage on sfpuc.org, and identify ways for better public outreach and education programs
Monitor and distribute incoming mail for Environmental Services and Field Services
Update and maintain staff sign in/out sheet and contact list
Manage Environmental and Field Services Cross Connection Control records in SharePoint
Submit Cross-Connection Control (CCC) Program updates for ES/FS staff meetings to the WQD Secretary
Submit Cross-Connection Control (CCC) Program updates for WQD Management Meetings to the WQD Secretary
Track paid and pending fines and service shutoff status for noncompliant accounts
Review, approve and assign new BPA’s entered into CCAMS
Order printed window envelopes from ReproMail
As needed (about once a year), order receipt books for backflow tag sales from ReproMail
Order backflow test tags
Performs other duties as assigned

Experience

How to qualify

One (1) year of clerical experience in a customer service, billing or collection department of a utility, bank, department store, Insurance Company, or credit agency.

added.description:
Position Description

Mission

The Mission of the Harris County Institute of Forensic Sciences is to provide medical examiner and crime laboratory services of the highest quality in an unbiased manner with uncompromised integrity.

Vision

To provide consistent, quality death investigation and laboratory analysis for the benefit of the entire community.
To create a technological strongpoint for legal agencies to facilitate justice in criminal and civil proceedings.
To establish an academic environment for training in the field of Forensic Science.

Brief Toxicologist 1 Overview:
The Toxicologist 1 is an early-career forensic toxicologist. This position is expected to operate analytical instrumentation, critically assess analytical data, report test findings, and render expert opinions and testimony in court primarily concerning tests performed by the laboratory.

Duties & Responsibilities:

Casework analysis and reporting: Performs toxicological analyses including ELISA, CO-oximetry, chemistries, ethanol and volatile quantitation with headspace GC/FID, and drug testing with GC/MS, GC/MS/MS, LC/MS/MS and/or LC/TOF MS instrumentation; critically evaluates instrumental data; reports results supported by analytical findings
Technical review of casework: Performs technical review of batch and case data to ensure compliance with laboratory procedures and accreditation standards
Laboratory support: Performs sample preparation techniques; receives, inventories and stores evidence; prepares test reagents and maintains supplies; performs laboratory upkeep duties
Result interpretation and testimony: Evaluates toxicology test results within case context. Testifies to analytical procedures performed; may testify to the effects of alcohol on human performance and behavior

Harris County is an Equal Opportunity Employer

https://hrrm.harriscountytx.gov/Pages/EqualEmploymentOpportunityPlan.aspx

If you need special services or accommodations, please call (713) 274-5445 or email ADACoordinator@bmd.hctx.net .

651.207

added.title: Assistant or Associate Professor - Environmental Chemistry and Contaminant Hydrology
added.description:
Working Title
Assistant or Associate Professor - Environmental Chemistry and Contaminant Hydrology

Department
School of Natural Resources-0844

Description Of Work

The School of Natural Resources at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln ( UNL ) Institute of Agriculture and Natural Resources ( IANR ) is seeking applications for an assistant or associate Environmental Chemistry and Contaminant Hydrology professor. Located in Lincoln, Nebraska, this 9-month (academic year), tenure-track appointment will explore how historical and current management in agricultural working landscapes affects the fate and transport of contaminants in the critical zone, including nutrient and pesticide legacies, agricultural and industrial chemicals, and/or emerging contaminants, and assess the vulnerability and resilience of soils, groundwater, and surface waters to these pressures. The apportionment is 50% research and 50% teaching.

Specific duties for this position are:

Applying core physical science expertise within environmental science (environmental geology, contaminant hydrology, environmental chemistry, ecological or environmental engineering, or similar) to advance understanding of contaminant fate and transport in the critical zone (Earth’s near-surface environment).
Working in collaborative research teams with a focus on Nebraska and region. Complement existing strengths of the School of Natural Resources, Conservation and Survey Division, and the Center for Resilience in Agricultural Working Landscapes ( CRAWL ), which include resilience theory, ecology, biogeochemistry, water science, geoscience, and cyberinfrastructure.
Teaching efforts will be dedicated to undergraduate education within the Environmental Science degree program in the School of Natural Resources. Develop innovative approaches to provide learning experiences while teaching annually Soils, Environment and Water Quality and Soils, Water, and Environmental Chemistry ; the candidate may teach additional introductory course as needed. The incumbent will be charged with mentoring to launch environmental science careers, including engagement with academic, industry and agency partners will inform workforce development and pathways to scientific careers through coursework taught. Development of workshops, pop-up courses, and/or digital badges is encouraged.

Recognizing that collaboration and participation in teams enhances creativity, innovation, impact, and a sense of belonging, the Institute of Agriculture and Natural Resources ( IANR ) and the School of Natural Resources are committed to creating learning, research, and Extension programming environments where the unique contributions of each individual are acknowledged and valued. At IANR we see every person and every interaction as important to our collective wellbeing and our ability to deliver on our mission.

Minimum Required Qualifications

Ph.D. in environmental science, water science, environmental chemistry, natural resources or a directly related field at the time of appointment.
Demonstrated ability to publish in appropriate peer‐reviewed journals.
Training and experience in environmental chemistry.
Experience or interest in working in agriculturally dominated landscapes of Nebraska and the Great Plains.

Preferred Qualifications

Demonstrated ability to obtain competitive extramural funding.
Experience in applying concepts of resilience, socio-environmental, or systems frameworks to address complex environmental problems.
Successful experiences teaching and/or mentoring undergraduate and graduate students.
Practical experience in disseminating information to a variety of stakeholders.
Postdoctoral, college/university faculty, or similar experience in environmental chemistry, hydrology, or related research.

added.description:
Overview

Department of Biosystems Engineering

Assistant Research Professor – Emerging Contaminants and Environmental Remediation

The Department of Biosystems Engineering of the College of Agriculture at Auburn University is seeking applications for the position of Assistant Research Professor in emerging contaminants and environmental remediation. This faculty position is a full-time, twelve-month, non-tenure track research appointment renewable annually, contingent upon satisfactory performance and funding. Full-time positions are eligible for benefits, including health insurance. The projected start date is June 1, 2027.

Responsibilities

The successful candidate will be responsible for developing an engineering research program focused on engineering sustainable remediation strategies using nature-based solutions and innovation treatment technologies to enhance environmental quality and resilience. The successful candidate will strengthen the collaboration with faculty involved in biochar systems, water resources, soil health, nutrient management, and ecosystem sustainability while expanding the department’s capacity in emerging areas of environmental concern. The successful candidate will exhibit excellent interpersonal and organizational skills in order to collaborate with other faculty members, staff, and stakeholders. In addition, the successful candidate will mentor biosystems engineering graduate and undergraduate students and produce scholarship through recognized peer-reviewed outlets, secure extramural funding to support his/her research program from external sources such as USDA-NIFA, NSF, and other related federal sponsors, and from relevant industries in Alabama and across the country.

Qualifications

Minimum qualifications are an earned Ph.D. from an accredited institution in biosystems, biological, agricultural engineering, or closely related engineering disciplines at the time employment begins. Candidates should demonstrate research experience in the area of environmental remediation for agricultural and biological systems, and have documented evidence of ability to conduct research work collaboratively with a variety of groups to include faculty, staff, stakeholders and graduate student colleagues. The incumbent must meet eligibility requirements for work in the United States at the time the appointment is scheduled to begin and continue working legally for the term of employment.

Desirable qualifications:
Demonstrated record of securing extramural funding for research or education programs and a strong record of publishing peer-reviewed journal articles.

Minimum Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

See above

Contract Type

Annual Appointment

Application Instructions

Applicants must apply for the position a nd upload the following: 1) a cover letter that addresses the experience pertinent to all of the position responsibilities, 2) a current curriculum vita, 3) copies of ALL academic transcripts, 4) a one to two-page statement of research philosophy and 5) Names, phone numbers and email for three professional references. CV and cover letter should be uploaded as one document under “resume” and all other documents should be uploaded under “additional documents”.
Only complete applications will be considered. To ensure consideration for the position, applicants must apply by January 4, 2027. Position may remain open until it is filled. Questions concerning the position should be directed to: Dr. Jasmeet Lamba, Search Committee Chair, email: lamba@auburn.edu

Company Description

Work with Us. Change the World.

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

AECOM
is seeking an Environmental Scientist I to be based in our Niceville, FL office. This position will support our Remediation team within our Environment business line. The Environmental Scientist I role t will provide field and office support on projects and will develop strong relationships with project managers and other technical personnel.

added.title: Environmental Specialist I, II & III
added.description:
Day in the Life of an Environmental Specialist:

As an Environmental Specialist I, II, or III on the Mid Atlantic field environmental team, you will apply technical expertise in air, water, chemical management, and/or waste. You will manage moderately complex projects and compliance programs that call for specialized, wide-ranging knowledge. Your day includes collecting operational data, submitting regulatory reports, conducting environmental sampling and testing, and participating in management of change processes to identify regulatory requirements. You will also serve as the point of contact for incident reporting, covering both event response and communication with regulatory agencies. You will track evolving regulations, such as updates to the Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, Resource Conservation and Recovery Act, Toxic Substance Control Act, Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act and guide operational changes to maintain compliance. The role also includes field engagements, training field staff, handling permit renewals and improvements, and working with engineering and operations teams on broader environmental initiatives.

Environmental Specialist I

Bachelor’s degree and 1+ year of related experience
Developing technical knowledge; routine permitting and compliance support 
Works with guidance; gathers data, maintains records, researches requirements, prepares routine submittals, and supports senior staff

Environmental Specialist II

Bachelor’s degree and 2+ years of environmental experience 
Functional knowledge across one or more environmental media; straightforward risk and compliance matters 
Works with increasing independence; provides guidance and training, coordinates routine permits, and prepares compliance reports and plans

Environmental Specialist III

Bachelor’s degree and 4+ years of environmental experience 
Technical expertise; moderate-complexity projects, programs, permits, audits, and risk matters 
Leads assigned work; recommends and implements risk responses, manages project scope/schedule/cost, improves programs, and builds agency relationships

Responsibilities/Expectations:

Develops, maintains and provides guidance on environmental processes/policies; conducts required environmental training
Assesses environmental risk, provides recommendations to address risk and participates in or handles the approved course of action, including required regulatory documentation
Participates in environmental project planning and implementation, including scheduling, cost estimating, preparation of environmental impact assessments and reporting
Prepares and submits sophisticated applications to procure environmental permits, renewals, approvals, variances, and other authorizations and coordinates with company partners
Performs environmental compliance audits and due diligence investigations, as the need arises
Develops, recommends and implements improvements for systems and practices in air, water, waste management and/or remediation activities for assigned areas

added.title: QC Microbiology Analyst (Environmental Monitoring)
added.description:
BeOne continues to grow at a rapid pace with challenging and exciting opportunities for experienced professionals. When considering candidates, we look for scientific and business professionals who are highly motivated, collaborative, and most importantly, share our passionate interest in fighting cancer.

General Description

Perform QC Microbiology environmental monitoring and laboratory activities to support GMP manufacturing, testing and release of materials, intermediates, and finished products under FDA/EU regulations, applicable International Regulations, BeOne processes and procedures. As a QC analyst, demonstrate proficiency and expertise in environmental monitoring for the site.

Essential Functions Of The Job

Support the QC Sr. Manager Environmental Monitoring in executing the site environmental monitoring program, including performance of monitoring activities, trending data, and managing material and media inventory.
Perform environmental monitoring of cleanroom suites and laboratory areas in accordance with the program direction set by the Microbiology leadership. Review EM data and write trend or summary reports to identify adverse microbial trends.
Required to gown into cleanrooms with different classifications and able to stand and move around for extended periods of time.
Support routine QC EM operations, including but not limited to: perform non-viable particulate, active and passive air viable, surface, and personnel monitoring. This includes monitoring during critical or aseptic processes, monitor and sample utilities such as WFI and purified water, including bioburden, endotoxin, TOC and conductivity testing to ensure timely generation and reporting of test results (for In-Process, Drug Substance, Drug Product, and Stability samples) in support of manufacturing operations, and support cleanroom qualification and requalification.
Support routine QC operations, including but not limited to: instrument qualification and maintenance, SOP generation and revision, trending reports, specification updates, record keeping and archival, etc.
Conduct investigations of OOS, discrepancies, errors, and failures, and escalate significant issues to the QC Microbiology leadership.
Participate in facility qualification activities for microbiological testing and utility and environmental monitoring.
Participate in internal and external GMP audits where possible.
Performs assigned activities in a manner to help ensure that the QC Microbiology laboratory meets or improves on budget, cost, volume, and efficiency targets (KPIs) in line with business objectives, as directed by the QC Sr. Manager Environmental Monitoring.
Undertake any other duties as assigned.

Core Competencies, Knowledge, And Skill Requirements

2+ years’ experience with Bachelor’s or above in Biology, Microbiology, or Biotechnology related scientific discipline, or 4+ years’ experience with less than Bachelors.
Working knowledge and experience with microbiological viable and non-viable EM sampling, compressed gas sampling, water sampling, and testing methods such as endotoxin, bioburden, sterility testing, microbial identification, biological indicators, plate reading, etc. as well as instruments such Incubators, Biosafety Cabinets, Plate Washers, and Microplate Readers, etc.
Knowledgeable with USP/EP and cGMP/EU GMP regulations.
Direct experience in a GMP quality control lab is a must.
Familiar with instrument and equipment validation.
Expert knowledge of quality control principles, practices, and standards for the biopharmaceutical industry.
Impressive, demonstrable track record and skills/experience gained within a similar position(s), at a similar level.
Credible and confident communicator (written and verbal) at all levels.
Strong analytical and problem-solving ability.
Excellent project management skills.
Hands-on approach, with a ‘can do’ attitude.
Ability to prioritize, demonstrating good time management skills.
Excellent attention to detail, with the ability to work accurately in a busy and demanding environment.
Self-motivated, with the ability to work proactively using own initiative.
Committed to learning and development.

Computer Skills

Strong PC literacy required; MS Office skills (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
Ability to work on a computer for extended periods of time.
Experience with Microbial LIMS is a plus

Travel

Must be willing to travel approximately 10%.

Global Competencies

When we exhibit our values of Patients First, Driving Excellence, Bold Ingenuity and Collaborative Spirit, through our twelve global competencies below, we help get more affordable medicines to more patients around the world.

Fosters Teamwork
Provides and Solicits Honest and Actionable Feedback
Self-Awareness
Acts Inclusively
Demonstrates Initiative
Entrepreneurial Mindset
Continuous Learning
Embraces Change
Results-Oriented
Analytical Thinking/Data Analysis
Financial Excellence
Communicates with Clarity
